description: Three-panel EIS figure for four low-density steel samples measured in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, with an identical legend in every panel: S0 (red stars), S950 (green circles), S1050 (blue triangles), S1150 (pink squares), plus black "fitting line" curves. (a) Nyquist plot, -Z_im versus Z_re, both axes 0-10000 Ω·cm², showing one depressed capacitive arc per sample with no Warburg tail; arrows marked "0.01 Hz" point to the high-frequency end of each arc. S950 gives the largest arc, reaching the 8000 Ω·cm² gridline on the real axis with a maximum -Z_im of roughly 4300 Ω·cm², whereas S0 gives the smallest (real-axis intercept near 5000 Ω·cm²); S1050 and S1150 fall between. An inset in (a) shows the fitted equivalent circuit: Rs in series with a branch in which Q1 sits in parallel with (R1 plus R2 in parallel with Q2). (b) Bode magnitude plot, |Z| (Ω·cm²) versus frequency (Hz), log-log from 10^-2 to 10^5 Hz and 10^0 to 10^5 Ω·cm²; the four curves merge above about 10^2 Hz (|Z| ≈ 10 Ω·cm²) and diverge at low frequency, where S950 is highest and S0 lowest. (c) Bode phase plot, -Phase (deg) 0-80 versus frequency, with one broad maximum near 70° at roughly 1-10 Hz, the S950 peak being shifted to lower frequency. Taken together, the panels rank S950 as the most corrosion resistant and S0 as the least.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a Nyquist plot with axes labelled Z_re (Ω·cm²) and -Z_im (Ω·cm²), both scaled 0 to 10000, showing a single capacitive arc for each of the four samples and no Warburg (45°) tail.

In the Nyquist plot the arc of S950 (green circles) is the largest, reaching the 8000 Ω·cm² gridline on the real axis, while the arc of S0 (red stars) is the smallest, with its real-axis intercept near 5000 Ω·cm²; S1050 and S1150 are intermediate.
An inset in panel (a) shows the equivalent circuit used for fitting, consisting of Rs in series with a network containing Q1, R1, Q2 and R2.
Arrow annotations reading '0.01 Hz' in panel (a) mark the high-frequency end of each capacitive arc.

Panel (b) is a Bode magnitude plot of |Z| (Ω·cm²) versus Frequency (Hz) on log-log axes (10^0-10^5 Ω·cm², 10^-2-10^5 Hz); all four curves overlap, falling from just below 10^4 Ω·cm² at 0.01 Hz to a plateau near 10 Ω·cm² above about 10^2 Hz.

Panel (c) is a Bode phase plot of -Phase (deg) versus Frequency (Hz) with the y-axis 0-80°; a single broad maximum close to 70° occurs at intermediate frequencies (about 1-10 Hz), and the S950 curve peaks at a lower frequency than S0, S1050 and S1150.
The legend shared by all panels lists exactly: S0 (red star), S950 (green circle), S1050 (blue triangle), S1150 (pink square) and fitting line (black line).
The caption identifies the three panels as (a) Nyquist plot, (b) Bode magnitude plot and (c) Bode phase plot of EIS curves recorded in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.

The citing text states that the Bode phase data show a superposition of two time constants with a maximum phase angle between 65° and 75° at intermediate frequencies, characteristic of nonideal capacitive behaviour, so constant phase elements Q are used instead of ideal capacitances C.

The citing text states that the equivalent-circuit parameters are Rs (solution resistance), R1/Q1 (ion diffusion resistance and CPE at the solution/film interface) and R2/Q2 (oxide film resistance and CPE), with Rp = R1 + R2.

The citing text reports fitted polarization resistances of 12486 Ω·cm² for S950 and 6036 Ω·cm² for S0, i.e. S950 approximately double S0; these values are given in Table 2 and are not printed in the figure.

The citing text states that the |Z| magnitude at 0.01 Hz is used to evaluate corrosion resistance, with S950 highest and S0 lowest at that frequency, consistent with the visual ordering of the low-frequency ends in panel (b).
The citing text asserts excellent agreement between experimental data and fitted curves in Fig. 8a-c, which is consistent with the black fitting lines tracking the coloured data points in each panel.

subfigures.description: Nyquist plot of -Z_im vs Z_re (both axes 0-10000 Ω·cm²) for S0, S950, S1050 and S1150 with fitted curves; each sample shows a single capacitive arc, S950 the largest (reaching the 8000 Ω·cm² gridline, max -Z_im ≈ 4300 Ω·cm²) and S0 the smallest. Arrows labelled '0.01 Hz' mark the high-frequency arc ends, and an inset contains the equivalent circuit Rs + [Q1 parallel with (R1 + R2||Q2)].

Bode magnitude plot: |Z| (Ω·cm²) on a logarithmic axis from 10^0 to 10^5 versus frequency 10^-2 to 10^5 Hz. All four curves nearly superimpose, decreasing from just below 10^4 Ω·cm² at 0.01 Hz to a plateau near 10 Ω·cm² above ~10^2 Hz; at low frequency S950 lies highest and S0 lowest.

Bode phase plot: -Phase (deg) from 0 to 80 versus frequency 10^-2 to 10^5 Hz, showing a single broad maximum near 70° at intermediate frequencies (about 1-10 Hz) for all samples, with the S950 maximum displaced to lower frequency and the curves converging above ~10^3 Hz to near 0-5°.
